candidates.name: Entergy
candidates.description: Both operate as large-scale integrated U.S. utility companies providing electricity to millions of customers.
candidates.rationale: Both are U.S. electric utilities operating large-scale power generation and distribution infrastructure for residential and commercial customers.

candidates.name: DTE Energy
candidates.description: Both are diversified energy holding companies managing regulated electric and gas utility operations in the United States.
candidates.rationale: DTE is a U.S. energy holding company operating regulated utilities and power infrastructure, closely overlapping NextEra’s core utility business and customer needs.

candidates.name: Alliant Energy Corporation
candidates.description: Both provide essential electric and natural gas utility services to residential and business customers across multiple states.
candidates.rationale: Both are regulated multi-state energy utilities providing electricity and investing in power generation and clean energy infrastructure for similar customer segments.

candidates.name: Evergy, Inc.
candidates.description: Both focus on the generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity within regulated utility markets.
candidates.rationale: Evergy is an electric utility engaged in power generation, transmission, and distribution, closely overlapping NextEra’s core utility operations and buyer ecosystem.

candidates.name: CenterPoint Energy, Inc.
candidates.description: Both manage critical energy infrastructure, including electric transmission and natural gas distribution networks.
candidates.rationale: Both are major electric utilities managing power generation or delivery infrastructure, with overlapping energy-sector customers, regulators, suppliers, and operational needs.

candidates.name: Avangrid, Inc.
candidates.description: Both are major U.S. energy providers with a significant emphasis on expanding renewable energy capacity.
candidates.rationale: Avangrid is an electric utility and renewable energy operator offering overlapping generation, transmission, distribution, and clean-energy infrastructure services.

candidates.name: Sempra
candidates.description: Both are prominent American energy infrastructure companies focused on large-scale utility operations and grid reliability.
candidates.rationale: Sempra is a large utility and energy-infrastructure operator with overlapping grid operations, power delivery, and institutional energy-market buyers.

candidates.name: Duke Energy Corporation
candidates.description: Both are among the largest electric utilities in the U.S. with extensive portfolios in power generation and distribution.
candidates.rationale: Duke Energy is a major electric utility with overlapping power generation, distribution, grid infrastructure, and clean-energy offerings serving similar energy-market buyers.

candidates.name: Southern Company
candidates.description: Both function as large-scale, integrated utility holding companies delivering electricity and gas to a vast customer base.
candidates.rationale: Southern Company is an integrated electric utility and power generator serving similar energy customers and infrastructure needs as NextEra Energy.

candidates.name: Dominion Energy, Inc.
candidates.description: Both operate as large-scale regulated utilities with significant investments in power generation and energy delivery infrastructure.
candidates.rationale: Both are electric utilities operating power generation and energy delivery infrastructure for substantially overlapping customer and procurement needs.

candidates.name: AEP
candidates.description: Both are leading electric utility companies with massive transmission networks and power generation capabilities across the U.S.
candidates.rationale: AEP is a major U.S. electric utility operating power generation and transmission infrastructure, directly overlapping NextEra Energy’s core business and buyers.

candidates.name: Xcel Energy, Inc.
candidates.description: Both operate as regulated utility companies providing integrated electricity and natural gas services across multiple states.
candidates.rationale: Both are multi-state regulated electric utilities with major power generation, transmission, and renewable energy operations serving similar customers and stakeholders.

candidates.name: FirstEnergy Corp.
candidates.description: Both are major investor-owned utilities focused on electric transmission, distribution, and grid management.
candidates.rationale: Both are investor-owned electric utilities operating major power transmission, distribution, generation, and grid infrastructure businesses for similar energy-sector stakeholders.

candidates.name: PSEG
candidates.description: Both serve as key utility providers for electricity and gas, maintaining critical regional energy infrastructure.
candidates.rationale: PSEG is an electric and gas utility operating power generation and regional energy infrastructure, closely overlapping NextEra’s utility business and buyer ecosystem.

candidates.name: Eversource Energy Service Company
candidates.description: Both operate as regulated utility providers focusing on the delivery of electricity and natural gas to residential and commercial customers.
candidates.rationale: Both are major regulated electric utilities operating power infrastructure and serving residential and commercial energy customers.

candidates.name: Ameren Corporation
candidates.description: Both are integrated utility companies dedicated to reliable power delivery and the management of regional energy grids.
candidates.rationale: Ameren is an electric utility operating power generation, transmission, and distribution infrastructure, closely overlapping NextEra’s core utility and grid operations.

candidates.name: WEC Energy
candidates.description: Both are large-scale energy holding companies that own and operate multiple electric and natural gas utility subsidiaries.
candidates.rationale: Both are utility holding companies operating electric power generation and delivery businesses, with overlapping infrastructure, regulatory, and enterprise buyer ecosystems.

candidates.name: PPL Foundation
candidates.description: Both function as regulated utility companies committed to providing safe, reliable energy delivery to millions of customers.
candidates.rationale: PPL Foundation is the utility company’s charitable arm, not itself an electric utility or clean-energy infrastructure operator.

candidates.name: PG&E Corporation
candidates.description: Both operate as major integrated utilities with extensive portfolios in electric power generation and distribution.
candidates.rationale: Both are major electric utility groups operating power generation, transmission/distribution, and clean-energy infrastructure for overlapping energy-market stakeholders.

candidates.name: Edison International
candidates.description: Both are large electric utility holding companies focused on energy delivery, infrastructure, and clean energy generation.
candidates.rationale: Both are electric utility holding companies operating power delivery infrastructure and clean-energy generation for substantially overlapping energy-market buyers and partners.

candidates.name: Constellation Energy Corp.
candidates.description: Both are major producers of clean energy and providers of large-scale retail and wholesale energy solutions.
candidates.rationale: Both are major power generators and energy suppliers offering clean energy and large-scale wholesale and retail electricity solutions to overlapping customers.

candidates.name: MidAmerican Energy Company
candidates.description: Both are utility companies providing integrated energy services with a heavy focus on wind and renewable energy investment.
candidates.rationale: Both are integrated electric utilities with substantial power generation, transmission, and renewable energy operations serving similar energy-market buyers and stakeholders.

candidates.name: Consolidated Edison, Inc.
candidates.description: Both are major regulated utility companies responsible for managing complex electric, gas, and steam infrastructure in high-density areas.
candidates.rationale: Both are major electric utilities managing power generation and grid infrastructure for utility customers, despite differences in geography and renewable-energy emphasis.

candidates.name: IDACORP, Inc.
candidates.description: Both operate as integrated electric utilities that prioritize regional energy reliability and grid infrastructure.
candidates.rationale: IDACORP is an integrated electric utility with overlapping power generation, transmission, grid infrastructure, and regional energy reliability operations.

candidates.name: Black Hills Corp
candidates.description: Both are investor-owned energy companies providing regulated electric and gas utility services to customers across multiple regions.
candidates.rationale: Both are investor-owned utilities operating electric generation and regulated energy distribution, serving similar customers and infrastructure buyers.
